title: Newton's Log-Concavity and Maclaurin's Inequality (OQ-02-OQ-02)
description: Proves Newton's log-concavity for elementary symmetric polynomials: (eₖ/C(n,k))² ≥ (eₖ₋₁/C(n,k-1))·(eₖ₊₁/C(n,k+1)). Derives Maclaurin's step Mₖ ≥ Mₖ₊₁. Both results derived as theorems (0 axioms). 15 theorems, 0 sorries, 0 axioms.

overview.historicalContext: Newton's inequalities (1707): (eₖ/C(n,k))² ≥ (eₖ₋₁/C(n,k-1))·(eₖ₊₁/C(n,k+1)) for elementary symmetric polynomials. Maclaurin's inequality (1729): M₁ ≥ M₂ ≥ ... ≥ Mₙ where Mₖ = (eₖ/C(n,k))^(1/k).
overview.problemStatement: Prove Newton's log-concavity and Maclaurin's step as theorems, eliminating the axioms in AmgmInequalityOQ02.lean.
overview.proofStrategy: 8-part proof: (I) structural properties, (II) unnormalized Newton eₖ² ≥ eₖ₋₁·eₖ₊₁ by induction, (III) binomial log-concavity, (IV)-(V) cleared-denominator induction, (VI) normalized Newton, (VII) power inequality aₖ^(k+1) ≥ aₖ₊₁^k, (VIII) Maclaurin step.
keyInsights: **Log-concavity via induction**: eₖ² ≥ eₖ₋₁·eₖ₊₁ proved by induction on n using the absorption identity eₖ(x₁,...,xₙ) = eₖ(x₁,...,xₙ₋₁) + xₙ·eₖ₋₁(x₁,...,xₙ₋₁).
**Cleared-denominator form**: working with C(n,k)²·eₖ² instead of normalized quantities avoids division and makes Lean's ring tactics applicable.
**Maclaurin from Newton**: each step Mₖ ≥ Mₖ₊₁ follows from Newton's inequality via the power inequality aₖ^(k+1) ≥ aₖ₊₁^k.

conclusion.summary: 15 theorems, 0 sorries, 0 axioms. Newton's log-concavity and Maclaurin's step proved from first principles.
conclusion.implications: Newton's inequalities are foundational in the theory of symmetric functions, with applications to correlation inequalities and unimodal sequences.
openQuestions: Can the full Maclaurin inequality chain M₁ ≥ M₂ ≥ ... ≥ Mₙ ≥ Mₙ₊₁ be formally proved?
Can Newton's inequalities be proved for general log-concave sequences?
Can the equality cases of Maclaurin's inequality be characterized?
